title: Immutable GPU nodegroup upgrade orchestration Terraform module (ASG + Karpenter interoperability)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a Terraform module for immutable GPU nodegroups in Private VPC that orchestrates safe rolling upgrades and interoperates with both ASG-based and Karpenter-managed provisioning. The module should prefer immutable replace-on-upgrade semantics, integrate driver/AMI preflight health checks, and expose knobs for canary batch sizes and conservative eviction windows. This ticket covers design, Terraform implementation, upgrade hooks, and a test plan for staged rollouts in staging and production-like environments.
background: Current GPU nodegroup modules allow in-place replacements that have caused intermittent driver mismatches and long-lived eviction windows during kernel/driver upgrades. We also have mixed fleets: some workloads still use ASG while newer clusters use Karpenter. Operators need a single Terraform abstraction that can create immutable groups (by creating new nodegroup stacks and draining old ones) and coordinate with Karpenter by tagging nodes and adjusting provisioning constraints during the window.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module creates named GPU nodegroup resource with immutable upgrade flag (default: true)
Upgrade plan flow: new nodegroup is provisioned, validated, traffic shifted, old nodes cordoned/drained and terminated
Module supports ASG-managed and Karpenter-compatible IAM tags/taints so provisioning tools can identify transitional nodes
Preflight health checks validate NVIDIA driver, CUDA version, and DKMS modules before marking node healthy
Canary upgrade parameter available (percentage or absolute count) and observed behavior documented
Module has automated rollback path: if healthchecks fail on >= X canary nodes, abort rollout and mark for manual review
Comprehensive example usage documented in README and a Terraform example repo for Private VPC
E2E test harness exists that simulates workload pods (GPU/FP16) and verifies inference latency before/after upgrade

decisions: Prefer immutable replace-on-upgrade semantics for nodegroups to avoid in-place driver drift
Expose a conservative default eviction window (30 minutes) with an override for low-latency workloads
Use Terraform null_resource local-exec to trigger k8s cordon/drain, but include a plan to migrate to controller-based orchestration later
For Karpenter, apply transitional tags: redwood.io/upgrade=true and redwood.io/upgrade-canary to influence provisioners
Healthchecks will be performed by a short-lived DaemonSet that reports results to a dedicated S3/Artifact endpoint readable by the module's CI checks
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Long drain windows increase cost. Mitigation: default small canary and configurable batch size; allow pre-warm pools for traffic-heavy services.
Risk: Karpenter may scale down canary nodes unexpectedly. Mitigation: apply node annotation to opt-out of scale-to-zero during upgrade window.
Risk: Driver install failing on specific GPU SKU. Mitigation: runner preflight image matrix test per SKU in staging before rollout to prod.
Risk: Terraform race conditions when deleting old ASG while Karpenter is reconciling. Mitigation: create explicit wait loops and confirm node absence via Kubernetes API prior to resource destroy.
testing_plan: Unit test: terraform validate, fmt, and module input permutations
Integration: spin up a staging cluster in Private VPC with mixed ASG+Karpenter provisioning and run a full replace upgrade with canary size=2
E2E: schedule GPU inference pods (TF-TRT and PyTorch) and assert latency P95 within 10% of baseline
Failure injection: simulate driver install failure and verify rollback path triggers and marks module state for operator review
Chaos: simulate node termination mid-drain and validate pod rescheduling into new nodes and surfacing of incidents in console
deployment_notes: Default behavior: immutable_upgrade=true; to opt into in-place behavior set immutable_upgrade=false
For Karpenter clusters, ensure controller version >= 0.25 and that IAM role allows DescribeInstances/Tagging for transitional tagging
Provide explicit terraform outputs: new_nodegroup_id, canary_node_ips, healthcheck_report_url
Operators should run terraform plan and address any drift (AMI changes, security groups) before applying
During rollout, monitor Console node health dashboard and per-route latency to detect regression early
